migration.name: 20261110063000_normalize_legacy_blocked_backlog
migration.backfill: Converts only historical BacklogItem.status=blocked rows to deferred. Each row retains its identity and receives a reason, observable resume trigger, 90-day review horizon, deferral timestamp, and active human owner resolved first from its submitting user and then through the governed platform-work owner chain. A status_change activity preserves the original value and decision provenance. The migration refuses to contract the column if any row cannot receive an owner, then replaces and validates the closed-set CHECK without blocked. No item is created, deleted, completed, or retired. Rollback is forward-only: application code can be reverted while the narrowed CHECK and preserved activities remain compatible; restoring blocked would require a new governed vocabulary expansion and is intentionally not automatic.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Historical blocked rows remain wanted work and move to the existing governed deferred lifecycle; non-blocked rows are unchanged. BacklogItemActivity retains the normalization event under the existing BacklogItem retention policy. The validated closed-set CHECK prevents reintroduction of the unowned status value; the parent enum-contract item retains the separate Prisma client conversion.

fields.reason: The canonical lifecycle already distinguishes actionable, awaiting-acceptance, done, deferred, and retired work. blocked was historical drift without the attribution required for parked demand, so the storage contract now enforces the canonical enum.
Each normalized row receives an active human Principal so the next review is attributable rather than hidden work debt.
fields.fieldPolicy: Store only the canonical Principal foreign key. Prefer the active principal linked to the original submitting user; otherwise use the existing platform-work accountability chain. Refuse the migration when no active human exists.

fields.reason: The migration states honestly that the historical blocker rationale was absent and requires current review before resumption.
The item resumes only after an accountable review records the actionable dependency or current scope and evidence.
A 90-day safety horizon prevents the normalized work from disappearing into indefinite deferral.
